Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following is the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$

examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $\mathbf T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/95c80fe2654c8f6eb4b65492eab1efb07f568375b2960b1633e5e2e1a7741a8b.png)
Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(3,-6), (1,-2),$ and $(-2,4).$  Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,-1),(0,-1),$ and $(0,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(4,-1)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(-4,-8)$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 & 0 \\ -8 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-4,-8),$ $(-1,-2)$, and $(0,0).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."
